speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms suggest a systemic issue; have you noticed any skin changes, rashes, or unusual bruising lately? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and peripheral smear. REQUEST IMAGES: Lymph node ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal; Lymph_Node_Ultrasound: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes observed.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of a fixed, painless, rapidly enlarging supraclavicular node combined with B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) is highly concerning for lymphoma. Given the urgency, I am proceeding with a tissue biopsy for definitive histology.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (suspected Hodgkin's or Non-Hodgkin's)
